newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes rise after ANS sold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast lt. crudes rise after ANS sold.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices rose Monday after a cargo of benchmark Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude sold at a smaller discount than previously, traders said.
Traders said a small asphalt-making plant bought a full cargo of ANS at $1.32 a barrel under June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, the benchmark U.S. grade.
The discount rose five cents from a April 30 deal between Chevron and Texaco, which saw barrels sell at minus $1.37.
Traders said the refinery paid up for ANS because the crude makes asphalt.
Demand for the viscous product is rising now that road repairs are underway for the summer.
Spot prices for WTI were flat from Friday at $19.55/19.65. The unchanged market and the tightening ANS discount combined to lift outright prices five cents to $18.18/18.38 a barrel.
Kern River and Wilmington, heavy California grades, eased after Texaco and Unocal lowered posted prices for the grade Friday.
Kern River crude fell 19 cents a barrel to $13.86/13.96 a barrel, while Wilmington shed 30 cents a gallon to $15.68/15.78 cents.
